A1.justification: Both PDFs describe LLM2Fx-Tools and contain complete, readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–G. Their content supports a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original reverse-engineering, style-transfer, natural-language-generation, and listening-test results, plus component and audio-encoder ablations (Tables 2–5 and Figure 4).

after.justification: v2 retains these original experimental results, including the listening test and appendix audio-encoder ablation.

M1.justification: Section 2 retains the same audio encoder, adapter, Qwen3-4B backbone, training losses, staged training, preprocessing, and tool-calling procedure. No method component changes.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same MedleyDB-derived LP-Fx data and MoisesDB/MedleyDB style-transfer evaluation. Reverse engineering, blind estimation, language generation, and listening-test coverage are unchanged.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in Tables 2–5, including the regression and MultiTask models, DeepAFx-ST, Gemini 2.5 Flash, Qwen language baselines, and audio-encoder alternatives.

E3.justification: Both retain the same splits, preprocessing, metrics, model configurations, and training budgets. Evaluation still uses 900 LP-Fx test conversations, 100 style-transfer samples, and a listening test with 16 participants and eight questions.

E4.justification: The CoT, Number Token Loss, and multi-stage-training ablations in Table 2, audio-encoder ablation in Appendix D/Table 5, and qualitative example in Appendix A are unchanged.

E5.justification: Figure 4 retains the same listening-score distributions, and Section 5.1 retains the same pairwise t-tests and significance reporting. Neither version adds run-count, seed, confidence-interval, or other uncertainty information.

E6.justification: All result entries and findings match, including Tables 2–5 and Figure 4. For example, Table 2 retains 80% classification accuracy, 0.56 ordering correlation, and 0.23 parameter MAE for LLM2Fx-Tools.

T1.justification: The task definitions, objectives, effect-composition formulation, assumptions, and metric equations in Section 2 and Appendices B/E are unchanged. No mathematical argument or proof is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about tool calling, CoT planning, multimodal control, LP-Fx, and experimental performance. The publication-header update does not alter these scientific contributions.

C2.justification: The interpretations in Section 5 and limitations in Section 6 are identical, including preprocessing-dependent interpretability, ambiguous effect-chain recovery, limited evaluation scale, single-instrument scope, and untested generalization to unseen effects.

D1.justification: Implementation and training details, dataset-generation instructions, prompts, sampling ranges, and resource URLs are unchanged. The added author email is a contact-information edit, with no revised code or data access instructions.

R1.justification: The cited works, bibliography, and positioning against prior research are unchanged. The ICLR publication designation and citation colors do not revise the paper's relationship to earlier work.

P1.justification: v2 replaces 'Preprint' with 'Published as a conference paper at ICLR 2026,' adds equal-contribution credit for Seungheon Doh and Junghyun Koo, and adds Koo's email. Research prose and section organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: v2 colors citation and hyperlink text, adjusts author and footnote formatting, and moves one introduction line from page 1 to page 2. Figures 1–4 and Tables 1–6 retain their content, structure, and placement.

improvement.justification: The revision updates publication metadata, attribution, and visual styling while preserving the scientific content throughout the main text and appendices. These limited editorial changes do not meaningfully alter the paper's evidential support, clarity, reproducibility, or overall quality.
